newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Wednesday with investors uncertain about the short-term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,175 yuan ($383) per tonne, losing 272 yuan. It opened at 3,180 yuan and hit a high of 3,182 yuan per tonne.
The contracts had fluctuated sharply this week on speculative trading ahead of delivery next week, traders said.
September rose 82 to 3,188, November put on 29 to 3,151, the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,160 and March fell 70 to 3,080. Combined volume fell to 16,100 tonnes from 22,400.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.

"Investors were mixed about the short-term market trend, making prices fluctuate sharply for the whole session," one trader said. "But the general outlook for soybeans is not optimistic due to weak physical prices."
Physical prices were around 2,900 yuan per tonne in the major producing areas in northeast China.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in the short term. ($1=8.2919 yuan)
